comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C2, C34, C35, C42. Both evaluations find the kinetic measurements of LRRK2's GTPase activity rigorous and well-supported, with reviewers explicitly praising the 'very careful biochemical analyses' and 'detailed accounting of catalytic efficiency.'

Perfect agreement on claims C3, C43, C44, C79. Both evaluations support the kinetic characterization of R1441G variant, with reviewers accepting these measurements as part of the rigorous biochemical analyses without challenge.

Strong agreement on claims C4, C45, C46 regarding G2019S kinetics. Both evaluations support these measurements as part of careful biochemical experiments. Peer review R3 does not explicitly mention C80, while OpenEval R3 includes it; however, peer R10 addresses C80 separately and supports it.

Perfect agreement on claims C47, C48, C49, C50, C51. Both evaluations strongly support the negative feedback mechanism demonstrated through kinase-dead and pharmacological inhibition experiments, with reviewers explicitly stating the feedback is 'convincingly demonstrated.'

Perfect agreement on claims C52, C53, C54, C55. Both evaluations support the ATP incubation experiments and the conclusion that autophosphorylation negatively regulates GTPase activity, with reviewers accepting the K1906M control as rigorous.

Agreement on claims C5, C58, C59, C60, C61 regarding T1343 as the critical phosphosite. Both evaluations support the mutational analysis data, though peer review does not explicitly address claims C56, C57 included in OpenEval R6. Reviewers accept T1343A data as consistent with phosphorylation-dependent mechanism.

Significant disagreement on claims C63, C64, C65, C66, C67. OpenEval finds the mass photometry data and mechanistic inference about oligomerization SUPPORTED, while peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, explicitly stating the 'regulatory mechanism directly linking the T1343 phospho-site and a monomer/dimer equilibrium is not fully supported' and conclusions are 'premature.'

Agreement on claims C6, C7, C8, C68, C69, C71, C72, C73. Both evaluations support the cellular and in vitro data showing T1343A effects on kinase activity and the lack of additivity with G2019S, though peer reviewers note limitations in extrapolating to cellular context.

Perfect agreement on claims C39, C40, C41. Both evaluations support the methodological validations and assay comparisons as part of rigorous experimental design, with reviewers praising the careful biochemical analyses.

Partial disagreement on claims C83, C84, C85. OpenEval rates computational modeling as UNCERTAIN due to lack of experimental validation, while peer reviewers rate it SUPPORTED as reasonable interpretation consistent with data, though both acknowledge the speculative nature of mechanistic claims.

Disagreement on claims C90, C91, C92, C93, C94, C95. OpenEval finds the mechanistic model SUPPORTED with appropriate caveats, while peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, stating the mechanism linking T1343 phosphorylation and monomer/dimer equilibrium is 'not fully supported' and requires independent validation.

Agreement on claim C97. Both evaluations support the main conclusion about negative feedback mechanism, with peer reviewers explicitly stating it is 'convincingly demonstrated,' though they note mechanistic details about oligomerization remain uncertain.

Agreement on claims C9, C78. Both evaluations rate the connection between kinetic parameters and clinical penetrance as UNCERTAIN/speculative. OpenEval notes lack of direct clinical data, while peer reviewers note the limitation that 'environmental context in cells cannot be captured from kinetic assays.'
Agreement on claim C70. Both evaluations support the cell-based assay results as confirmatory data consistent with published findings. Peer R10 also addresses C80 which OpenEval includes in R3.

OpenEval R12 addresses claims C86, C87, C88, C89 regarding database information and literature context (Rab24 parallel). These literature-based contextual claims are not explicitly evaluated separately in peer review results, though they may be implicitly accepted as background.

OpenEval R15 addresses extensive background claims C1, C10-C38, C74-C77, C81-C82, C96 from the literature. These established background claims are not separately evaluated in peer review results, as they represent cited prior work rather than new findings requiring validation.
